lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Ah, welcome back! I've swapped my trowel for a telescope tonight; the sky is <color=red>exceptionally</color> clear.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: I've drafted a short piece on astronomy, but five words have drifted off into the <color=red>void</color>. Restore them, and five new books will touch down in the library.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text:
Missing word 1:
With no air to carry its vibrations, sound cannot <color=red>_____</color> through the vacuum of space.
lines.hint: Not quite. You need a word meaning 'spread' or 'travel'.
lines.correctText: With no air to carry its vibrations, sound cannot <color=red>propagate</color> through the vacuum of space.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text:
Missing word 2:
Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, <color=red>_____</color> Venus is actually the hottest, thanks to its thick, heat-trapping atmosphere.
lines.hint: Not quite. You might expect the closest planet to be hottest, but it isn't. Which word signals that surprise?
lines.correctText: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, <color=red>yet</color> Venus is actually the hottest, thanks to its thick, heat-trapping atmosphere.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text:
Missing word 3:
Saturn's rings are not solid; they are composed of <color=red>_____</color> chunks of ice and rock.
lines.hint: Not quite. Rings made of many separate pieces need a word meaning 'a huge number'.
lines.correctText: Saturn's rings are not solid; they are composed of <color=red>countless</color> chunks of ice and rock.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text:
Missing word 4:
Aboard the space station, astronauts experience near <color=red>_____</color>, so they must strap themselves in to sleep.
lines.hint: Not quite. Why would someone need straps to stop them drifting away?
lines.correctText: Aboard the space station, astronauts experience near <color=red>weightlessness</color>, so they must strap themselves in to sleep.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text:
Missing word 5:
The first footprints on the Moon remain <color=red>_____</color>, since there is no wind or rain to erase them.
lines.hint: Not quite. If nothing erases them, what state are they still in?
lines.correctText: The first footprints on the Moon remain <color=red>intact</color>, since there is no wind or rain to erase them.

lines.speaker: Gus
lines.text: Superb. My essay is complete, and five new volumes are making their <color=red>descent</color> towards the library.

afterLines.speaker: Gus
afterLines.text: Thank you again. Do look in on the library, then return one clear night and we'll <color=red>stargaze</color> together.
